catalog_quote: [p.19] The language has three level tones and two contours. It is also a stress accent language, and while stress is often predictable, in many instances it must be lexically encoded. ... [p.40, 2.3.2 Stress] In addition to contrastive tones, MacZ also has phonemic stress, as indicated by the near minimal pair in 29, in which the first word has initial stress, indicated by the double uu, while the second word has stress on the final diphthong, indicated by the doubled ii. 29. guudia gúdììà C/bathe P/write have bathed will write Although these words differ in tones, this difference does not condition the difference in stress. Instead, stress must be lexically specified. [p.41] There is some interaction between stress and tones, but these are largely independent of one another. ... [p.42] As noted, tones do not serve as a direct cue to stress. In fact, there does not seem to be a consiste…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all quoted segments (p.19, sec. 2.3.2 pp.40-42, pp.45-46, sec. 2.4.2 pp.52-53) found verbatim in the held Foreman 2006 PDF/text at the stated locators. (2) Deciding source: a 661-pp UCLA dissertation that Glottolog ranks as the languoid's grammar, with a dedicated stress section containing a near-minimal stress pair, an explicit 'stress must be lexically specified' statement, the root-bound/default-initial generalisation, and the author's own duration measurements — first-hand, modern, variety-specific. Our 'lexical' coding (root-bound phonemic stress, default first syllable of a disyllabic root, contrastive root-final stress) is a faithful reading. sources.citation: Barzilai, Maya L. & Kate J. Riestenberg. 2021. Context-dependent phonetic enhancement of a phonation contrast in San Pablo Macuiltianguis Zapotec. Glossa: a journal of general linguistics 6(1): 69. DOI 10.5334/gjgl.959 (open access).
sources.quote: No stress rule is stated; stress is treated as a lexical property marked per word in transcription ('capitalized tone levels indicate the stressed syllable'; IPA ˈ on e.g. ˈjè.là 'night', ˈʂú.dí 'father' vs unmarked-initial gú.sàʔ 'mud'), and distributional statements presuppose both stressed and unstressed root syllables: 'Modal and checked vowels can appear in both stressed and unstressed syllables, while VʔV ... would be restricted to stressed syllables in root-final position, as in belaʔa'. Also: 'MacZ, however, retains post-tonic vowels and allows plenty of disyllabic roots'. Cites Forema
